merger_description:
Sheffield TopCo Pty Ltd, a member of the group of companies trading as Sheffield Group (**Sheffield**), proposes to acquire the business and all of the assets of Champion Parts Pty Ltd, trading as Champion Fasteners (**Champion Fasteners**) (the **Acquisition**).

Sheffield is an Australian wholesaler of hand tools, abrasives and power tool accessories predominantly supplying industrial wholesale and retail customers.

Sheffield is majority-owned by Seidler Equity Australia II, LP (**Seidler Australia**), a private equity fund advised and/or managed by affiliates of Seidler Equity.

Seidler Equity is a private investment firm specialising in providing long-term equity capital to family-owned businesses across Australia with a presence in the United States. Within Australia, Seidler Equity holds interests in various other industries, including consumer products, professional services, and business services.

Champion Fasteners is an Australian wholesaler of fasteners, fittings and tools predominantly supplying automotive wholesale and retail customers.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Sheffield (and Seidler
Equity’s wider portfolio) and Champion Fasteners in the
supply of fasteners and fittings in Australia
b. while there is small horizontal overlap between Sheffield and
Champion Fasteners in the supply of hand tools, power tool
accessories and abrasives in Australia, the parties’
combined share is low and the increase in share of supply
arising from the Acquisition would be small
c. there are alternative suppliers of fasteners, fittings, hand
tools, power tool accessories and abrasives in Australia
d. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of the relevant products post-
acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
